newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO CHIEF REPORTED IN BRIBE PROBE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO CHIEF REPORTED IN BRIBE PROBE.

text.p: The chairman of soccer champions Porto, Jorge Nuno Pinto da Costa, and two directors are being investigated over the club's payment of a holiday in Brazil for a leading referee, Portuguese media reported on Friday.
The reigning champions have admitted that they picked up a 700,000 escudos ($4,600) bill for the holiday for referee Carlos Calheiros in the summer of 1995 but say that it was paid by mistake.
According to the TSF radio station and the Bola sports daily, police put Pinto da Costa and two other club directors formally under investigation after questioning them in Porto on Thursday.
Club officials were not available to comment on the reports.
Porto, who are looking to win a record third successive league title this season, are also involved in another probe into alleged match-fixing.
UEFA is probing allegations by a Portuguese businessman that he was asked to act as a middleman in an attempt to bribe a referee before a European Cup game with Scotland's Aberdeen in 1984.
Porto has strongly denied the accusations made by Fernando Barata, a former chairman of the Farense soccer club.
